verdict.rationale: Pipedream's docs say you can write Node.js 'at any point of a workflow,' with npm packages and the $.export helper for passing data between steps. Its GitHub README says workflows can run Node.js, Python, Golang, or Bash code, and community users confirm workflows are code and welcome the Python support. Missing for 10: a dedicated first-party Python code-step doc page in the evidence (Python support rests on the README and community comments rather than in-depth docs).

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop into real code (JavaScript or Python) as a step inside a workflow

citations.quote: Pipedream supports writing Node.js v at any point of a workflow. Anything you can do with Node.js, you can do in a workflow.
Pipedream allows you to run any Node.js, Python, Golang, or Bash code. You can import any package from the languages' package managers
you can use pre-built components when you're performing common actions, but you can write custom code when you need to.
Python support and the key/value store is super cool to see.
